At 10 p.m. 30/3/36 D.S.87 Jones, D.S.I. Shih
Sou Chien and C.D.S.155 attached to the Special
Branch together with D.S.I. Yao Yuen Loong and
C.D.S.253 attached to Kashing Road Station raided
an upstairs back room at Lane 244 House No.9 Sing-
keipang Road on the authority of a S.S.D.Court
Search Warrant No.9461 dated 30/3/36, on informa-
tion obtained by C.D.S.155 attached to the Special
Branch to the effect that membersof the Communist
party were residing in a back room above the
kitchen and that the occupants of the room in ques-
tion were in possession of communistic literature.

When the Police party entered the back room
above the kitchen the only occupant was a male
Chinese who gave his name as Tsang Kyien Ming
(章健民) age 21, Native of Shaoshing, S/Coolie,
residing at Lane 244, House No.9 Singkeipang Road.

A search was made of the room and the following
literature of a communistic nature was seized
in various parts of the room.

1) The Shao Nian Zhen Li Bao (the Youth Truth Pao)
(少年真理报) a Communistic paper, Issue No.111. 320
copies.

2) A manifesto issued by the Central Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party to the people
throughout the country. 45 sheets.

3) A manifesto issued by the Kiangsu Provincial
Committee of the Chinese Communistic Youth
Group supporting the strike of the workers of
the Dah Kong Cotton Mill (大康纱厂).

36年3月30日晚上10点，隶属于特务科的侦探警佐（D.S.）87号 Jones、侦探督察（D.S.I.）施守坚（Shih Sou Chien）和刑事侦探警士（C.D.S.）155号，连同隶属于嘉兴路巡捕房的侦探督察姚元龙（Yao Yuen Loong）和刑事侦探警士253号，根据1936年3月30日签发的特区法院搜查令第9461号，搜查了辛家坊路244弄9号厨房楼上的一间后屋。此次行动基于附属于特务科的刑事侦探警士155号所获情报，即共产党员居住在厨房上方的一间后屋内，且该房间的居住者持有共产主义文献。

当警察小队进入厨房上方的后屋时，屋内只有一名华人男子，他自称 Tsang Kyien Ming (章健民)，年龄21岁，籍贯绍兴（Shaoshing），职业/苦力，居住于辛家坊路244弄9号。

对该房间进行了搜查，并在房间各处查获以下具有共产主义性质的文献。

1) 《少年真理报》(The Shao Nian Zhen Li Bao / the Youth Truth Pao)，一份共产主义报纸，第111期。320份。

2) 中国共产党中央委员会向全国人民发布的宣言。45张。

3) 中国共产主义青年团江苏省委员会发布的宣言，支持大康纱厂工人的罢工。

T Tsang Kyien Ming 章健民 ) 1st accused.
Shaoshing, Chekiang. D.S. Jones
Kashing Rd Stn 30/○/36. D.S.I. Shih Ssu Chien

My name is Tsang Kyien Ming 章健民). I am a
native of Shaoshing, Chekiang Province, age 21 years. At
the age of seven years I began to attend the primary school
at Shaoshing, but as my father is a small farmer without
much money I had to leave school after only two weeks of
study and help till the land. I continued to assist my father
on the farm until I was 16 years old, and then left home and
came to Shanghai. Through the influence of my brother I got
a job with a silk factory in Nantao. This job I held for
six months and then left of my own accord because of the death
of my grandmother, and returned home. I stayed at home help-
ing my father until July 1935, when I returned to Shanghai
in search of employment. I lived with my brother in Zikawei
Road, French Concession until the Chinese New Year (January)
1936), when X my brother returned to Shaoshing . At about
this time I obtained a job as operative in the Pao Hwa (宝華)
Silk Manufactory, Yue Wo Faung (月華坊), Ward Road. I was
employed there for two months after which I was thrown out
of employment owing to a change of management. During the
time I worked at the Pao Hwa silk manufactory I lived in
an adjoining alleyway. After a short visit to Hangchow, where
I went in search of a job, I returned to Shanghai and took up
my present place of abode at House No.9, Lane 844 Singsinpeng Rd.

I do not know the man who was arrested in the alleyway
shortly after my own arrest and I do not know why the said tenant
stated that he was my room-mate. I have never seen him before.

The communist literature found in my room was left there

T Tsang Kyien Ming 章健民 ) 第一被告。
浙江绍兴。D.S. Jones
嘉兴路站 30/○/36。副巡长 Shi Ssu Chien

我叫 Tsang Kyien Ming（章健民）。我是浙江省绍兴人，现年21岁。七岁时，我开始在绍兴读小学，但因父亲是个贫农，没钱供我读书，我只读了两周便辍学回家帮家里种地。我一直帮父亲干农活直到16岁，随后离家来到上海。在我哥哥的影响下，我在南市的一家丝厂找到了一份工作。这份工作我做了六个月，后来因为祖母去世，我主动辞职回家。我留在家里帮助父亲，直到1935年7月，我再次回到上海寻找工作。我和哥哥一起住在法租界的高恩路（Zikawei Road），直到中国新年（1936年1月），当时 X 我的哥哥回到了绍兴。大约在这个时候，我在华德路（Ward Road）月华坊（Yue Wo Faung）的宝华（Pao Hwa）丝织厂找到了一份操作工的工作。我在那里工作了两个月，后因管理层变动而失业。在宝华丝织厂工作期间，我住在附近的一条弄堂里。在去杭州短暂寻找工作未果后，我回到上海，并搬入现在的住址：新闸路（Singsinpeng Rd.）844弄9号。

我不认识在我被捕后不久在弄堂里被捕的那个人，我也不知道为什么该房客声称他是我的室友。我以前从未见过他。

在我房间里发现的共产主义文献是我的一个名叫 Tsang Lien Sung（张连生）的朋友留下的，

Szechuan
D.S.I. Yao Yuen Loong.
K.Rd. Station 30/3/36

My name is Zee Vung Ming. I am 25 years old and am a native of Szechuan. I am residing at Lane 120/5 Tatung Road, Chapel. I studied in the Tsung Tung School in Szechuan for about 2 years. When I was 17 years of age, my father died. In March, 1935, I arrived in Shanghai for the purpose of obtaining a job.

After arriving in Shanghai, I resided at No.25 Si Zung Li, Rue Brenier de Montmorand, French Concession, for about 2 months. In May 1935, I obtained a job as a coolie at the Zung Vang Contractor, Shanhaikwan Road, I stayed there until my services were terminated in November, 1935.

After that I removed to Lane 120/5 Tatung Road, Chapel. I have since been unemployed.

I was arrested in Lane 244 off Singkeipang Road.
I could not identify the other man arrested.
I knew nothing of the books and papers seized by the Police.

I am not a member of the Communist Party and do not belong to any other political party.

It is not true that I live with the other person arrested at House No. 9, Lane 244 Singkeipang Road. I have never seen the man before in my life.

Zee Vung Ming. 徐文虹
四川
副巡长 Yao Yuen Loong。
K路警局 30/3/36

我叫 Zee Vung Ming。我今年25岁，是四川人。我居住在 Chapel 区大同路（Tatung Road）120弄5号。我在四川的宗通学校（Tsung Tung School）学习了大约两年。我17岁时，父亲去世了。1935年3月，我来到上海找工作。

到达上海后，我在法租界白尔尼埃·德·蒙莫朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）思仲里（Si Zung Li）25号居住了大约两个月。1935年5月，我在山海关路的 Zung Vang 承包商处找到了一份苦力的工作，我一直工作到1935年11月被解雇。

之后，我搬到了 Chapel 区大同路120弄5号。此后我一直失业。

我是在新闸路（Singkeipang Road）旁244弄被捕的。
我无法指认另一名被捕男子。
我对警方查获的书籍和文件一无所知。

我不是共产党员，也不属于任何其他政党。

说我与新闸路244弄9号被捕的另一人同住是不实的。我这辈子从未见过这个人。

Charge Application is hereby made by the S.M.Police to the S.S.D.Court for the detention of the above two described male Chinese under Arts. 76 and 101 of the C.P.R.C. arrested at about 10.15 p.m. 30.3.36 in Lane 244 House No. 9 Singkeipang Road, on suspicion of being memeber of the Communist party.
IN THE SECOND BRANCH KIANGSU HIGH COURT A.M.
Mr. Kum appeared for the S.M. Council.
Proceedings. Mr. Kum:- Your Honour. The two accused are suspected of being concerned in the communist activities, so the Police apply for the detention. At 10 p.m. on the 30/3/36 members of Special Branch and Kashing Road Station raided premises at Lane 244, House No. 9 Singkeipang Road. Before raiding the house, C.D.S. 155 of the Special Branch received information to the effect that the premises in question was a communist organ. Based on this information a Search Warrant Nos. 9461/1419 (handed in and kept by judge) was applied for and executed. In the kitchen room the 1st. accused was arrested with a seizure of some literature (list describing the communistic books etc produced). The 1st. accused stated that the seized literature was notbelonged to him. It was owned by one named Tsang Lien Sung who has gone to Nanking. In the course of searching, C.D.S. 155 was kept a watch in the rear door when the 2nd. accused was coming in. He was taken into custody. The chief tenant Lee Sze stated that the two accused were living together in the kitchen which was hired and paid by the 1st. accused. In the Station the two accused failed to recognise each other and denied participating in the communist party. On arrest, the 2nd. accused was found to have three pieces of paper relating to the question of ricksha pullers etc, throwing into his mouth. This was stopped by the detectives and the paper were taken out from the mouth of the 2nd. accused (paper produced). As further enquiries are necessary, I ask

Q. Did the 2nd Accused particularly point out the
house to you ?
A. Yes, he said that he had lived there.
2nd Accused:- I did live there before, but I removed
out since 20/3/36. Since then I could not afford to hire any
house but lived in a small lodging house. Later my friend gave
me a paper slip and told me to see a man named Tseu Shing in the
alleyway on Singkeipang Road. I was then arrested.
Judge to Fee Tung Sz:- Are you the chief tenant of
the House No.9 Lane 244 Singkeipang Road ?
Fee Tung Sz:- Yes.
Q. Have you any relation to the 1-2 Accused ?
A. No. On 19/2/36 they removed in. The 1st Accused
first came alone to hire the place saying that he was working in
a factory and his name was Tsang. He added that one more friend,
i.e. the 2nd Accused, would live together with him. On the day
of the removal into our house, both the 1st and the 2nd Accused
came together. They went out and came back through the back door
so I did not know much about them.
Q. Did many friends come to see them ?
A. No, not many friends, so far as I knew.
Q. Had any other one paid a visit to them ?
A. I don't know. They used to go out together.
Q. Did any one named Tsang Lien Sung live in your
house ?
A. No.
1st Accused:- Yes, I knew Tsang Lien Sung through
the introduction of my brother.
Judge to 2nd Accused:- According to the chief
tenant, you did live in her house.

Proceedings. Mr. Kum:- He outlined the case. At 10.15 p.m. 30.3.36,
Police acting on the authority of S.S.D.Court Search Warrant
went to No 9 Lane 244 Singkiepang Road, where the 1st. accused
was arrested, and a quantity of literature of Reactionary nature
was seized. The 2nd. accused was arrested when he went to the
house. The chief tenant stated that the 2nd. accused rented the
room in which the 1st. accused was arrested. Both accused denied
being the occupants of the room. Police have made a list of the
seized property, pamphlets etc, and the same has been handed into
Court. Both accused are charged under article 2 and 6 of the C.C.C.
1st. accused:- I admit occupying the upstairs rear
room at No 9 Lane 244 Singki pang Road, it was rented by Tsang
Lai Sung. He left a box in the room. I first met Tsang Lai Sung
when I was employed in a silk filature in Nantao, he told me that
he could get me better employment in a new factory. Tsang Lai Sung
went to Hankow and left the box and his property in the room, he told

MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. S. B. REGISTRY
734
Subject Examination and Listing of Communist Literature and Documents
seized at No. 239 Myburgh Road.
Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by D.S.J. Jones
All literature and documents seized during the course of
the raid conducted by the Special Branch on the communist base
discovered at No. 239 Myburgh Road have now been thoroughly
examined and a completely revised list - made necessary by the
discovery that certain of the books and documents in question
bore messages and notes written in sympathetic ink - drawn up.
(Copies of revised list attached to this report).
In my report dated April 1st I advanced the theory that
the Communist Youth League had probably had a hand in the student
disputes affecting Chinese universities in general, and the
Futan University in particular.
Document No. 78 on the revised list lends support to this
theory. The following three slogans taken from the document
in question prove that the Communist Youth League is not only
interested in the Futan University students dispute but is
seeking to exploit the present unrest among the students:-
(1) Demand the immediate release of the arrested Futan
University students.
(2) Demand the punishment of persons responsible for shooting
the students.
(3) Demand the payment of medical expenses incurred by the
students.
All names appearing in the documents seized during the
raids carried out at the addresses in Pingliang and Myburgh
Roads have been noted for future reference. Certain names and
addresses of "comrades" allegedly residing in Chinese territory
have been passed to the Chinese authorities for investigation.
Results of any action taken by the latter will be made known
later.

734
主题：对在迈尔赫路（Myburgh Road）239号查获的共产主义文献和文件的检查与列单
制作人：D.S. Jones 转发人：D.S.J. Jones
特别科在对发现于迈尔赫路（Myburgh Road）239号的共产主义据点进行的突袭行动中查获的所有文献和文件，现已经过彻底检查，并编制了一份完全修订的清单——之所以需要修订，是因为发现某些书籍和文件上载有用隐形墨水书写的信息和笔记。（修订后的清单副本附于本报告后）。
在我4月1日的报告中，我提出了一种理论，即共产主义青年团可能插手了影响中国各大学，特别是复旦大学的学潮。
修订清单上的第78号文件支持了这一理论。从该文件中摘取的以下三条标语证明，共产主义青年团不仅关注复旦大学的学生纠纷，而且试图利用当前学生中的动荡局势：
(1) 要求立即释放被捕的复旦大学学生。
(2) 要求惩办枪击学生的责任人。
(3) 要求支付学生产生的医疗费用。
在平凉路（Pingliang）和迈尔赫路（Myburgh Road）各地址进行的突袭行动中查获的文件中出现的所有姓名，均已记录在案以备将来参考。据称居住在中国境内的某些“同志”的姓名和地址已移交给中国当局进行调查。后者采取任何行动的结果将在日后公布。

A considerable amount of writing in sympathetic ink
concealed in the pages of a Chinese book entitled "Education
and Profession" was brought to light by the use of chemical
reagents and a full translation of this writing made by the
staff of S.2 (Vide Exhibit No. 15 attached). Examination of
hidden writing thus revealed shows that it was adopted to
preserve from prying eyes the secret signs and passwords used
by communist agents as a method of precaution when meeting
one another on streets or in public places previously agreed
upon; to indicate the form advertisements should take when
using the columns of the Press as a medium for the dissemination
of notices and warnings in code; and to outline the procedure
to be followed when an agent is unable to keep a rendezvous due
to his being shadowed. Many names and addresses were found
inscribed in sympathetic ink on the pages of this book and on
other scraps of paper found among the seized literature. The
majority were Chinese names and addresses, but there were also
a few foreign names, not the least important of which was that
of the well known newspaperman and radical, F. C. Glass. This
is not the first time that the name of Glass has appeared on
documents seized in raids on Communist bases in Shanghai (Vide
File No. 1771 on Glass). Beyond the bare mention: "Glass
resides at 177 Avenue Dubail" (the name and address was written
in English; while the two words RESIDES AT were in Chinese
characters) nothing was found in the said documents to indicate
what connection - if any - Glass had with the communist suspects
arrested. Another foreign name written in sympathetic ink
and made visible by applying a chemical reagent was that of

通过使用化学试剂，在一本名为《教育与职业》的中文书页中隐藏的大量隐形墨水字迹被显现出来，并由第2股工作人员进行了全文翻译（见附件第15号）。对 thus 揭示的隐藏字迹的检查表明，其目的是为了防止秘密信号和密码被窥探，这些信号和密码是共产主义特工在预先约定的街道或公共场所会面时作为一种预防措施而使用的；用于指示在使用报刊栏目作为传播编码通知和警告的媒介时，广告应采取的形式；并概述了当特工因被跟踪而无法赴约时应遵循的程序。在这本书的书页以及在查获文献中发现的其他纸片上，发现了许多用隐形墨水书写的姓名和地址。大多数是中国人的姓名和地址，但也有少数外国人的姓名，其中最重要的之一是著名记者和激进分子 F. C. Glass。这并非 Glass 的名字首次出现在上海共产主义据点突袭行动查获的文件中（参见关于 Glass 的档案号 1771）。除了简略提及：“Glass 居住在杜白尔路（Avenue Dubail）177号”（姓名和地址用英文书写；而 RESIDES AT 这两个词用汉字书写）之外，在上述文件中未发现任何内容表明 Glass 与被捕的共产主义嫌疑人有任何联系（如果有的话）。另一个用隐形墨水书写并通过施用化学试剂而显现的外国人名是 AUSLANDER，居住在北京路83号。Auslander 是

notorious Jewish moneylender of Rumanian nationality.
All Chinese names and addresses appearing in Exhibit No.15
have been investigated by detectives attached to this Section.
In every instance, excepting one, either the name or the idress
was found to be fictitious. The exception is that of HSIA
TSUNG YUAN (夏春元), of the Compositors' Room, Dah Tsing
Printing Establishment(大晶), Ningpo Road. When enquiries
were instituted at this printing shop, which is situated at
No. 659 Ningpo Road, it was ascertained that a native of Zangchow
named Hsia Tsung Yuan had been employed there as a type-setter
for about one year. According to the information obtained,
this man left Shanghai for his native place some two weeks ago
on private business. The date of his return is uncertain.
Exhibit No. 54 consists of a series of six letters likewise
written in sympathetic ink (vide full translation attached),
bearing on the communist situation in Kwangse, and containing
instructions for developing and intensifying communistic
activities in that province. These letters indicate the
communist base raided by the Police at No. 239 Myburgh Road to
be the Publication Department of the Provincial Committee of
the Communist Youth League and show that it was also used as a
clearing house for reports sent by communist agents in the
interior.

附件第15号中出现的所有中国姓名和地址均已由隶属于本股的侦探进行调查。除一例之外，在所有情况下，要么姓名要么地址被发现是虚构的。唯一的例外是大晶印刷所（Dah Tsing Printing Establishment，位于宁波路）排字房的夏春元（HSIA TSUNG YUAN）。在对这家位于宁波路659号的印刷店进行查询时，查明一名来自常州（Zangchow，音译，应为常州）名叫夏春元的人已在那里担任排字工约一年。根据获得的信息，此人约两周前因私事离开上海返回家乡。其返回日期不确定。

List of Communist Literature seized from room over kitchen,
219 Alyburgh Road, at 10 P.M. APRIL 1, 1936

1) A report made by Lee (李), dated April 1, 1936,
relating to organization problems of the Communist
Party.
This document accused Lee Vung Shing attempted to throw
away when the Police entered his room.

2) An envelope dated April 1, addressed to Hsu Kwah Sien (許魁先),
105 Zung Chong Li, Pingliang and Yangtsepoо Roads.
This envelope was found on desk.

3) A letter dated March 28, signed Ih Sing (伊生) (name of
recipient not given) dealing with the general principles
of the reorganization of the Cultural Committee and other
communist problems . (found in a book on desk).

4) Pro-communist periodical entitled "Giu Guo Sh Bao", issue
No.11, dated 4/2/36, written in Chinese and published in
Paris.                                                                 19 copies.

5) Booklet entitled "Stories on Various Anniversaries".
This booklet contains a brief sketch of various
anniversaries which are being observed by the
communists.

6) A booklet containing the synopsis of a drama entitled
"To enlarge the red army".

7) A booklet published in 1933 containing several articles
concerning the activities of the Communist Youth
International.

8) A booklet published in December, 1935 containing several
articles describing the "Western Expedition" of the Red
Armies and three maps showing the route of the "expedition".

9) A booklet published on August 17, 1934 containing
articles dealing with the International Youths Anniversary
(September 1), the departure of Red Armies for North
to Resist Japan, etc.

10) A booklet entitled "The Construction of the Soviet".
One of the articles contained in this booklet announces
that Soviet Russia has joined the League of Nations
with the intention of making the League a tool to further
her socialistic propaganda.

11) A booklet entitled "Matters to be studied" published
by the "China Leftists Cultural League" on December 20,
1934.
This booklet contains articles dealing with the
"popular revolution" and the situation in the Chinese
literary circles.

12) A booklet entitled "Songs for Mass Propaganda" containing
a number of songs for mass propaganda.
This booklet contains principles of cultural work
of a literary nature.

13) A book entitled "Political Work in the Red Army" published
in 1934, 1935.

14) A book entitled "History of Political Service of Soviets"
(Volume II).

6) 一本小册子，包含一部题为《扩大红军》的戏剧的剧情简介。

7) 一本出版于1933年的小册子，包含几篇关于

page_data.en:
Translation of Exhibit No. 54, consisting of
6 letters written in secret ink, seized at
239 Myburgh Road on April 1, 1936.

(1)

March 30.

(Name of recipient not mentioned),

The following are some of our important
tasks to be carried out at present:-

(a) Extend the anti-Japanese and anti-Chiang (Chiang
Kai Shek) movement laying stress upon opposition
to the Emergency Mandate and the suppression of
24 different kinds of publications; carry out
propaganda work, such as the issue of circular
telegrams and protests, demanding the release
of the students of the Fudan University who have
been arrested.

(b) Enforce national salvation education, adopt the
"small teacher system", and organize peasants'
book reading classes in order to get into touch
with peasants.

(c) Advocate the cessation of civil war and the
commencement of an anti-Chiang war.

(d) Direct peasants in opposing payment of taxes and
rentals.

(e) Enlarge our membership and form a united front of
various cliques.

(Signed) Bah Ying(白英).
------------------

(2)

March 30.

Comrade Bah Pee(白波),

(1) The address we gave you on a previous occasion was
cancelled recently. We did not receive any letter
from you. Is there any important report in your
previous letters?
page_data.zh:
证物第54号译文，由6封用密写墨水书写的信件组成，于1936年4月1日在迈尔堡路（Myburgh Road）239号查获。

(1)

3月30日。

（未提及收件人姓名），

以下是我们目前要执行的一些重要任务：-

(a) 扩大抗日和反蒋（蒋介石）运动，着重反对《紧急治罪法》以及对24种出版物的查禁；开展宣传工作，如发布通电和抗议书，要求释放被捕的复旦大学学生。

(b) 推行救国教育，采用“小先生制”，并组织农民读书班，以便与农民取得联系。

(c) 倡导停止内战，开始反蒋战争。

(d) 指导农民抗税抗租。

(e) 扩大我们的成员队伍，组成各派系的统一战线。

（签名）白英 (Bah Ying)。
------------------

(2)

3月30日。

白波 (Bah Pee) 同志，

(1) 我们前次给你的地址最近已取消。我们没有收到你的任何来信。你之前的信件中是否有重要报告？

page_data.en:
-2-
(2) Have you received the documents and books which
we sent to the Woo Jan (烏橋小学) Primary School
during that period?
(3) Important and complicated matters to be reported
to Shanghai in person, and letters to be sent
only in cases of emergency.
(4) Have you seen Comrade Ziang (翔)? We have not
heard from him for a long time.
(5) The National Salvation Newspaper, published in
Paris, is very good. Please push its "sale."
(6) We are short of money here. Please send a
suitable amount every month to the new communication
address.
(7) Carry on your work independently. Let us know if
you have any difficulty.
(Signed) Bah Ying.
----------------
(3)
March 31.
Chih Jui (潔如),
We have received your letter addressed to Comrade
Chuan Fang (傳芳). We told you on Feb. 1 that we did
not receive your letter; this is true. Our address
in Route des Sieyes was cancelled sometime ago. Does
your letter contain any addresses or important messages?
Please pay attention to it. For the time being let
your letters be sent to us through Comrade Chuan Fang.
We will let you know as soon as we have a new address.
Please write reports by secret methods (meaning to write
in secret ink) and give us your address to where we
can send "The Truth of Youth Newspaper" so as to enable
you to understand the recent policies. If possible
please supply us some funds for expenses. Your letter
was mailed on March 18/
(Signed) Lee Tseung ...

(2) 你是否收到了我们在那段时间寄到乌桥小学 (Woo Jan Primary School) 的文件和书籍？
(3) 重要且复杂的事项需亲自向上海汇报，仅在紧急情况下才寄送信件。
(4) 你见过翔 (Ziang) 同志吗？我们很久没有他的消息了。
(5) 在巴黎出版的《救国报》很好。请推动其“销售”。
(6) 我们这里资金短缺。请每月向新的通讯地址发送适当金额。
(7) 独立开展工作。如有困难请告知我们。
（签名）白英 (Bah Ying)。
----------------
(3)
3月31日。
洁如 (Chih Jui)，
我们收到了你写给传芳 (Chuan Fang) 同志的信。我们在2月1日告诉过你，我们没有收到你的信，这是事实。我们在西耶斯路（Route des Sieyes）的地址不久前已取消。你的信中是否包含任何地址或重要信息？请注意这一点。暂时让你的信件通过传芳同志转交给我们。一旦我们有新地址，会立即通知你。请用秘密方法（意指用密写墨水书写）撰写报告，并告知我们可以寄送《青年真理报》的地址，以便让你了解近期的政策。如果可能，请提供一些经费。你的信是3月18日寄出的/
（签名）李增 (Lee Tseung) ...

page_data.en:
-3-

(4)

March 31.

Comrade Sing Ming(新民),

We shall investigate your failure to receive
our letters sent since January and hope you will also
look into it.

Your last secret letter is not clear. We agree
to your proposal to come to Shanghai for discussions on
work but we do not regard it advisable for you to read
books for two months as you cannot be away from Kwangsi
for so long. If you decide to come, we will assist
you financially. Let us know the date of your arrival
and the hotel in which you are going to stay, so that we
will send a man to meet you.

You have got into touch with the Party in Kwangsi.
You must make a very careful inspection of the Party
organizations, read their documents and guard yourself
against traitors. Start a movement in Kwangsi to demand
the release of the Futan students, and support the
students movement in Peiping by holding demonstrations.

Let us know whenever you receive literature from
us so as to assure that nothing is lost. Please push
the "sale" of the National Salvation Newspaper openly,
and if you have a bookstore as communication address the
paper may be sent to you direct from France.

Please submit a detailed report on party
organizations in Kwangsi. Carry out your work in
accordance with the principles published in the Truth of
Youth Newspaper.

(Signed) Sing Jen(新人)

-3-

(4)

3月31日。

新民 (Sing Ming) 同志，

我们将调查你未能收到我们自一月份以来寄出的信件的原因，希望你也对此进行调查。

你最后一封密信不清楚。我们同意你来上海讨论工作的提议，但我们认为你像计划那样读书两个月是不可取的，因为你不能离开广西那么久。如果你决定来，我们将在经济上资助你。请告知我们你的抵达日期以及你将入住的旅馆，以便我们派人去接你。

你已与广西的党组织取得联系。你必须非常仔细地检查党组织，阅读他们的文件，并提防叛徒。在广西发起一场运动，要求释放复旦学生，并通过举行示威游行支持北平的学生运动。

每当你收到我们寄去的文献时请告知我们，以确保没有遗失。请公开推动《救国报》的“销售”，如果你有一家书店作为通讯地址，报纸可以直接从法国寄给你。

请提交一份关于广西党组织的详细报告。按照《青年真理报》上发表的原则开展工作。

（签名）新人 (Sing Jen)

Chiang movement and the student movement in which a demand
be made for the release of the Futan students arrested
in Shanghai. For methods of work please refer to the
Truth of Youth Newspaper and other documents.

page_data.en:
Translation of article in French found among communist
literature seized at No.239 Myburgh Road.

Life in Prison

The Prison : Last year this prison was handed over to the
Nanking Government, but the power is still in the hands of the
French imperialists. The occupants of the gaol are arrested and
handed over by the French Police. Everything in the prison
depends on French imperialists. This is the reason why the
prisoners in this prison are much worse treated than those in
other prisons. When the prison belonged to French imperialists
there were only 800 prisoners; now there are more than 2000.
In this we see that the Kuomintang, in order to keep in with
the imperialists, endeavours to persecute the people. The
prison can only contain 800 prisoners, but now it is more than
a third (sic). During the present hot weather eight men are shut
up in a little room where they cannot stretch their legs. The
air is insupportable; the meals are very bad. Nine-tenths are
sick. In winter there is no mattress underneath and no covering
on top. All day one hears nothing but the noise of blows with
the fists and batons, and the groans of the sick.

The Life : For food we are paid 16 sous a day; but owing to the
grafting habits of the Director of the prison, we don't draw so
much as 10 sous a day. The rice we eat is mixed with many other
things; with pieces of very bad vegetable. It is said that one
can eat meat, but the meat supplied often causes terrible sickness.
One is allowed only one bath a week and one wash a day. Eighteen
hundred people wash in the same water. The one who washes last
has to use water which gives off the same vile odour as that in
street sewers. A man is set to watch the water and whenever
anyone approaches for a wash he shouts "Quickly! Quickly! Quickly!"
Three minutes only is allowed for a wash. Some who come to dip
their hands in the water are driven away, beaten or insulted.
Five times a week we are allowed 15 minutes for recreation, but
we do not always get this 15 minutes. But the White Russians
are given recreation six times a week, each period of recreation
lasting one hour and a half. Not only are they better off in
this respect, but they are also allowed 70 sous a day for food.

Persecution : Not only do the prisoners live wretchedly, they
also undergo terrible treatment. Robbers are usually tied by the
legs at the order of the French imperialists. Practically every
day they are beaten on the hands and feet with sticks. If they
try to defend themselves they are persecuted in the manner
handed down by Chinese ancestors. Last year a poor wretch who
broke an ordure bucket was punished in this fashion. Many others
also receive this same punishment. Many commit suicide. On May 6
last year a prisoner, tying his legs with No. 181 named
CHANG WA SIN because of a serious illness spoke wildly being
known by the Chief of Police and the Secretary of the Prison;
they stopped the poor wretch up with iron and the next day he
had lost four teeth (sic). He lost much blood and not long
after he was dead. His comrade in the prison kept the four
teeth as a souvenir. To end our misfortune we do not know that
it is necessary to crush all imperialists and the Kuomintang.

Sickness and Death : It is through the bad situation and the
persecution that nine tenths of the prisoners are sick. The
page_data.zh:
在迈尔西爱路239号缴获的共产主义文献中发现的法文文章译文。

监狱生活

监狱：去年这座监狱移交给南京政府，但权力仍掌握在法国帝国主义者手中。监狱的囚犯由法国警察逮捕并移交。监狱的一切事务都取决于法国帝国主义者。这就是为什么这座监狱的囚犯受到的待遇比其他监狱的囚犯差得多的原因。当监狱属于法国帝国主义者时，只有800名囚犯；现在有2000多名。从中可以看出，国民党为了迎合帝国主义者，竭力迫害人民。监狱只能容纳800名囚犯，但现在超过了三分之一（原文如此，意指超额拥挤）。在目前炎热的天气里，八个人被关在一个小房间里，连腿都伸不直。空气令人难以忍受；饭菜非常糟糕。十分之九的人都病了。冬天下面没有床垫，上面没有被子。整天听到的只有拳打脚踢的声音和病人的呻吟声。

生活：我们的伙食费每天16苏（sous），但由于监狱长的贪污习气，我们每天领到的不到10苏。我们吃的米饭里混有许多其他东西；夹杂着很坏的蔬菜碎片。据说可以吃肉，但供应的肉经常导致严重的疾病。每周只允许洗一次澡，每天洗一次脸。一千八百人在同一盆水里清洗。最后洗的人不得不使用散发出与街道下水道同样恶臭的水。有人专门看守用水，每当有人接近洗脸时，他就大喊：“快点！快点！快点！”洗脸只允许三分钟。有些来把手浸在水里的人被赶走、殴打或侮辱。每周允许我们有五次、每次15分钟的娱乐时间，但我们并不总能得到这15分钟。但是白俄每周有六次娱乐时间，每次娱乐持续一个半小时。他们不仅在这方面待遇更好，而且每天的伙食费也高达70苏。

迫害：囚犯们不仅生活悲惨，还遭受可怕的待遇。强盗通常按照法国帝国主义者的命令被绑住双腿。实际上，他们每天都要被棍棒殴打手脚。如果他们试图自卫，就会受到中国祖先传下来的方式的迫害。去年，一个可怜的倒霉蛋因为打碎了一个粪桶而受到这种惩罚。许多其他人也受到同样的惩罚。许多人自杀。去年5月6日，一名编号为181的囚犯张华新（CHANG WA SIN，音译）因重病胡言乱语，被警长和监狱秘书知晓；他们用铁器堵住了这个可怜人的嘴，第二天他就掉了四颗牙齿（原文如此）。他失血过多，不久后就死了。他在狱中的同志保留了这四颗牙齿作为纪念。为了结束我们的不幸，我们必须粉碎所有帝国主义者和国民党。

疾病与死亡：正是由于恶劣的环境和迫害，十分之九的囚犯患病。

page_data.en:
(2)

rrison doctor has stated that two thirds of the prisoners have tuberculosis and skin disease. There is only one doctor for 1800 prisoners. This is the reason why a sick person will go without food and cry out for several days without a doctor going near him. Usually if one becomes seriously ill one dies. On an average there is a death a day. Everybody weeps over this. When almost dead one is sent to the St Marie hospital belonging to the French imperialists. There is an average of one death a day among the patients of this hospital. During the hot weather there are often five deaths a day. We are told by prisoners who have been in hospital that the foreign doctor will not come near the patient if he is a prisoner, except, perhaps, once a month, when he looks at the patient for about ten minutes and then goes away. Sick prisoners fear the St Marie hospital as though it were a human slaughterhouse. Even when gravely ill one is not willing to go into this hospital.

The conflict of the Prisoners : To protect their lives all the unfortunates in prison get together and oppose persecution. On March 17 of this year everyone gave a united shout to oppose persecution. This shout terrified the Police of the French Concession and they sent a large number of their men to watch us. The Director of the prison yielded to our agitation and accepted all our demands. Not long after, though, four hundred of our comrades were sent to other places far from Shanghai. On August 1st 1933the Director was changed. The new Director was worse than the old. Many are persecuted. We cannot talk out loud. On August 24, 1933 a prisoner on the 2nd floor was put in another room and had his legs tied and feet fastened. All the comrades on the 2nd floor got very angry and shouted loud their protests. The Director, more terrible than ever, tied the legs of three others. On the evening of the same day all prisoners on the 2nd and 4th floors were tied by the legs and they all shouted loudly together. The Director ordered all the Police to strike and kick. At this moment only groans and cries of suffering could be heard. Persecution such as this is not only to be found in prisons but in the whole of China.

The life of the gaolers and police : Altogether there are more than forty police and sixty gaolers in the prison. Most of these come from villages. Some took part in the revolution of 1927. They spend a laborious life. The monthly salary is about ten dollars. When absent through sickness a deduction is made from their salary. They get no time off for holidays. They follow one-another on day and night duty and they have to do other work. They can be punished or dismissed by their superiors. There is no bed in which they can sleep and their food is bad. In addition there are thirty men employed to take the place of those absent. These get their food but no wages. They are good, especially to political prisoners. Not long ago they requested an increase of salary; that a bed be supplied, and that special work be abolished. Their request for a bed was granted, but the bedhas not yet been supplied.

Continuation of life in Prison : During recreation if one talks or moves the head one is punished terribly. At the start and finish of the recreation xxxx or before going for a bath, it is not permitted to stand upright. There are 600 prisoners at work. Tailoring and weaving is done. Match boxes are made, things for scholars in bamboo, wood; paper boxes, printing. The work lasts 12 hours a day, but not a sou is paid in wages. Some of the prisoners have their legs bound during the work. When working more than one hundred prisoners are confined in a room and guarded by dozens of gaolers. Everything is done by the prisoners. From morn to sunset they are at work. As the work is of a laborious nature and no wages are paid those who work are given food a little better than that given to those who do not work.

(2)

监狱医生声称，三分之二的囚犯患有肺结核和皮肤病。1800名囚犯只有一名医生。这就是为什么病人会断食并哭喊数日，却无医生前来看视的原因。通常，一旦病重就会死亡。平均每天有一人死亡。众人对此无不悲泣。当人濒临死亡时，会被送往属于法国帝国主义者的圣玛丽医院（St Marie hospital）。该医院的病人平均每天死亡一人。在炎热天气里，往往每天死亡五人。据住过医院的囚犯告诉我们，如果病人是囚犯，外国医生就不会靠近他，除非也许每月一次，他会看病人约十分钟，然后离去。生病的囚犯害怕圣玛丽医院，仿佛那是人间屠宰场。即使病重，也不愿进入这家医院。

囚犯的斗争：为了保命，狱中所有不幸者联合起来反对迫害。今年3月17日，大家齐声高呼反对迫害。这呼喊吓坏了法租界警察，他们派遣大量人员监视我们。监狱长屈服于我们的抗争，接受了我们的所有要求。然而不久之后，我们的四百名同志被送往远离上海的其他地方。1933年8月1日，监狱长更换。新监狱长比旧的更坏。许多人受到迫害。我们不能大声说话。1933年8月24日，二楼的一名囚犯被关进另一间房间，双腿被绑，双脚被固定。二楼的所有同志都非常愤怒，大声抗议。监狱长变本加厉，又绑了另外三人的腿。当天晚上，二楼和四楼的所有囚犯都被绑住双腿，他们一起大声呼喊。监狱长命令所有警察殴打踢踹。此刻只能听到痛苦的呻吟和哭喊。这样的迫害不仅存在于监狱中，也遍及全中国。

狱卒和警察的生活：监狱中共有四十多名警察和六十多名狱卒。这些人大多来自农村。有些人参加了1927年的革命。他们过着劳苦的生活。月薪约为十元。病假要扣薪。节假日没有休息。他们日夜轮班，还要做其他工作。他们可能受到上级的惩罚或解雇。他们没有睡觉的床铺，食物也很差。此外，还有三十人被雇用来顶替缺席者。这些人有饭吃但没有工资。他们人很好，尤其是对政治犯。不久前，他们要求增加工资；提供床铺；并取消特殊工作。他们关于床铺的请求已获批准，但床铺尚未提供。

监狱生活的延续：在放风期间，如果说话或转头，就会受到严厉惩罚。在放风开始和结束时 xxxx 或在去洗澡之前，不允许直立站立。有600名囚犯在工作。从事裁缝和编织工作。制作火柴盒、竹木文具、纸盒、印刷品。每天工作12小时，但不支付任何工资。部分囚犯在工作期间双腿被绑。工作时，一百多名囚犯被关在一个房间里，由数十名狱卒看守。一切工作均由囚犯完成。从早到晚他们都在工作。由于工作性质劳累且无工资，做工的人得到的食物比不做工的人稍好一些。

page_data.en:
(3)

Formerly prisoners did not have the privilege of sending
letters, reading and writing, or receiving visitors. Now things
are a little better. Political prisoners are kept apart. Formerly
they led a different life to that of ordinary prisoners. After
a year of struggle, it is now permitted to read, consult a
doctor, bath and drink water.

Continuation of Persecution : Number 110 LI CHIN AN witnesses the
death of CHANG WA SIN. On August 30 last year the following were
terribly assaulted : Nos. 102, 207, 126, 176, 74, 22, 217, 63, 84
and 29; while the following were persecuted in Chinese fashion :
Nos.52, 125, 121 and 209. Number 67 testified that No.175 died
as the result of persecution. Nos. 15 and 110 testified that
No.181 was killed. No. 193 testifies that No.188 died in prison
for want of medical attention. The head gaoler who came at the
same time as the new Prison Director is extremely ferocious.
Often political prisoners are punished by being left without food
for three or four days. For talking one political prisoner was
punished by being deprived of food for 8 days.

Because of the resistance of the prisoners, especially on
account of the shouting of all prisoners at 12 midnight, they
are preparing to persecute us more severely.

--------------
page_data.zh:
(3)

以前，囚犯没有寄信、读写或接待访客的特权。现在情况稍有好转。政治犯被单独关押。以前他们的生活与普通囚犯不同。经过一年的斗争，现在允许阅读、看医生、洗澡和喝水。

迫害的继续：110号李金安（LI CHIN AN）目睹了张华新（CHANG WA SIN）的死亡。去年8月30日，以下人员遭到残酷殴打：102号、207号、126号、176号、74号、22号、217号、63号、84号和29号；而以下人员遭受中式迫害：52号、125号、121号和209号。67号作证说，175号因迫害而死。15号和110号作证说，181号被杀害。193号作证说，188号因缺乏医疗护理死于狱中。与新监狱长同时来的首席狱卒极其凶残。政治犯常因被罚禁食三四天而受惩处。一名政治犯因说话被罚禁食8天。

由于囚犯的抵抗，特别是因为所有囚犯在午夜12点的高呼，他们正准备更严厉地迫害我们。

Tsui Tih Sung (朱铁生) began to have connections
with the "Chiao Lien" (Educational League) about two years
ago, when he lost touch with "Central" and requested a member
of the League named Ling, a native of Chekiang, to transfer
his communications to "Central".
Ling is said to be an ex-communist. Ling, Tsui and
another named Zung, a native of Chekiang, once worked together
for a long period. The book entitled "Criticisms on Materialism
and Experience" was translated by Tsui and Zung together
under the pen names, Tih Sung (铁生) and Dih Sing (笛秋).
The letter (?Tsui's letter to Central) was delivered
to the "Tang-Tuan" (Branch of Communist Party and Youth League
in subsidiary organizations) of the Educational League, but
Tsui was still unable to find "Central". Subsequently Ling
induced Tsui to reside in a "small library" which has connections
with the Educational League. After residing there for a consi-
derable period, during which he was kept under the observation
of members of the Educational League, Tsui, being guaranteed
by Ling, was sent to Postung to work on farm lands and wharves.
He proved himself a capable and hard working comrade, and was
then transferred to the Educational League as a member of its
standing committee. At that time one Lau Soeng (老宋) was
also a member of the standing committee. Soeng maintained his
personal relationship with an ex-member of the standing commit-
tee named Lau Yui (老余), and once Lau Yui told Soeng that Tsui was
a "traitor". As Yui was unable to produce any evidence, Tsui
was kept on the committee and there was nothing suspicious
about his daily work.
After working with the Educational League for three or
four months, Tsui succeeded in re-establishing connections
with "Central" and then left the League. About the summer of
last year Tsui suddenly went to a place connected with the
Educational League stating that he had just returned from the
page_data.zh:
1936年4月1日在迈尔赫路（Myburgh Road）239号查获的第1号证物译文。（这份文件是李永兴（Lee Vung Shing）在被捕时试图销毁的）。
----------------------------------------
朱铁生（Tsui Tih Sung）大约在两年前开始与“教联”（Educational League，即教育联合会）建立联系，当时他与“中央”失去联系，便请求教联一名姓凌的浙江籍成员将其通讯转交“中央”。
据说凌是一名前共产党员。凌、朱以及另一名浙江籍姓宗（Zung，音译）的人曾长期一起工作。《唯物主义和经验批判主义》一书由朱和宗以笔名铁生和笛秋（Dih Sing，音译）共同翻译。
这封信（？朱给中央的信）被递交给教联的“党团”（Tang-Tuan，附属组织中的共产党和青年团支部），但朱仍无法找到“中央”。随后，凌引诱朱住进一个与教联有联系的“小图书馆”。在那里住了相当长一段时间后，期间一直受到教联成员的监视，朱在凌的担保下，被派往浦东（Postung，音译，应为浦东）在农田和码头工作。他证明自己是能干且勤奋的同志，随后被调入教联担任常务委员。当时，老宋（Lau Soeng）也是常务委员之一。老宋与前任常务委员老余（Lau Yui）保持个人关系，有一次老余告诉老宋，朱是“叛徒”。由于老余拿不出任何证据，朱留在委员会中，其日常工作并无可疑之处。
在与教联工作三四个月后，朱成功恢复了与“中央”的联系，随后离开了教联。去年夏天左右，朱突然去了一个与教联有关的地方，声称他刚从北方回来。

page_data.en:
-2-

North. He wrote a letter requesting the Educational League
to approach the Central on his behalf and also requested
Lau Soong to get him into touch with the "Central," which
Soong did. Lau Soong at that time was undertaking Party
activities in the Eastern District of Shanghai. His defect
is his inclination towards the Trotsky Clique. He has not
made any improvement despite repeated advice.

Sometime ago Lau Tsui endeavoured to take over
"Party connections" from Lau Soong but this was opposed by
Lau Yui. Lau Tsui also declared that the Party had the
intention to stop activities in "White" districts owing to
difficulties. For these reasons Lau Soong and Lau Yui
became suspicious of Lau Tsui, and thought him to be an
impostor. These suspicions were cleared up when Tsui's
report to Central was handed to us, showing that he is
actually connected with the Central.

I wish to point out that although Lau Tsui has
made a number of mistakes in his work, there is no evidence
to prove that he is a "spy". The facts contained in his
report to the Central are true, and he would not be able
to write such a report should he be an impostor. As regards
his incorrect statement that the Party will stop activities
in White territory, we can clear it up by observing his
practical work.

Lee, April 1, 1936.

-2-

他写了一封信，请求教联代表他与中央接洽，并请求老宋帮他联系“中央”，老宋照办了。当时老宋正在上海东区从事党的活动。他的缺点是有倾向托洛茨基派系的倾向。尽管多次劝告，他仍未改正。

前一段时间，老朱（Lau Tsui，此处指朱铁生，原文混用Lau/Tsui）试图从老宋手中接管“党的关系”，但这遭到老余的反对。老朱还宣称，由于困难，党打算停止在“白区”的活动。出于这些原因，老宋和老余对老朱产生怀疑，认为他是冒牌货。当朱给中央的报告交给我们后，这些疑云得以消除，报告显示他确实与中央有联系。

我要指出的是，虽然老朱在工作中犯了一些错误，但没有证据证明他是“间谍”。他给中央报告中的事实是真实的，如果是冒牌货，他写不出这样的报告。至于他关于党将停止在白区活动的错误说法，我们可以通过观察他的实际工作来澄清。

李，1936年4月1日。

File No. D. 7340
Special Branch S.2.
REPORT
Date April 2, 1936

Subject Arrest of Communist suspects at No. 9, Lane 244 Singkeipang Road
and No. 239 Myburgh Road.

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by D.S.J.

Examination of the various documents seized during the
course of the raids carried out at the above addresses makes it
apparent that the two communist suspects arrested on March 30th
at Singkeipang Road and the two apprehended at Myburgh Road are
either members of, or connected in some way with, the Chinese
Communist Youth League. Before any action was taken to accomplish
their arrest these four prisoners, who were suspected of being
engaged in communist activities, were kept under observation and
shadowed by agents under the supervision of C.D.S. 155 attached
to this Section. On one occasion C.D.S. 155 saw one of the two
suspects who was taken into custody at No. 9 Singkeipang Road in
company with one of the men arrested at No. 239 Myburgh Road. This
fact may be regarded as a strong indication that not only these
two, but all four of the men detained are closely connected and
probably engaged in the same illegal activities.

A much greater quantity of radical literature was found at
the address raided in Myburgh Road than at Singkeipang Road,
where the first warrant was executed. It is highly probable that
the two Myburgh Road suspects occupy a more responsible position
in the Communist Youth League than the two arrested at the
address in Singkeipang Road. For one thing, they appear to belong
to a better class; then again, they are obviously better educated.

When the party of Police headed by D.S. Jones entered the
room over the kitchen occupied by the two accused at No. 239
Myburgh Road, a man, who later gave his name as Lee Yung Shing
(李永兴), rose from the table at which he was seated and made
frantic efforts to destroy a small handwritten document which he
had been perusing. An examination of this document showed that
it dealt with Party matters and the activities of certain members

主题：在新嘉坡路（Singkeipang Road）244弄9号和迈尔赫路（Myburgh Road）239号逮捕共产党嫌疑犯。

制作人：D.S. Jones 转发人：D.S.J.

对上述地址突击搜查过程中查获的各种文件的审查表明，3月30日在新嘉坡路逮捕的两名共产党嫌疑犯和在迈尔赫路抓获的两名嫌疑犯，要么是中国共产主义青年团的成员，要么以某种方式与其有关联。在采取行动实施逮捕之前，这四名涉嫌从事共产党活动的囚犯一直处于本分部所属的C.D.S. 155号警探的监督下，由特工进行监视和跟踪。有一次，C.D.S. 155号警探看到在新嘉坡路9号被捕的两名嫌疑犯之一，与在迈尔赫路239号被捕的一名男子在一起。这一事实可被视为强烈的迹象，表明不仅这两人，而且所有四名被拘留者都密切相关，并且可能从事相同的非法活动。

在执行第一张搜查令的新嘉坡路地址，查获的激进文献数量远少于在迈尔赫路被突击搜查的地址。迈尔赫路的两名嫌疑犯在中国共产主义青年团中担任的职位可能比在新嘉坡路地址逮捕的两名嫌疑犯更为重要。一方面，他们似乎属于更好的阶层；另一方面，他们显然受过更好的教育。

当由D.S. Jones率领的警察队伍进入迈尔赫路239号两名被告所占用的厨房上方的房间时，一名后来自称李永兴（Lee Yung Shing）的男子从他就座的桌旁站起来，疯狂地试图销毁他一直在阅读的一份小型手写文件。对该文件的检查显示，它涉及党务和某些成员的活动

of the Chinese Communist Party, some of whom were connected
with "Central". (Vide full translation of document attached).
    While the raid at No. 239 Myburgh Road was in progress,
D.S. Jones and Clerk Zung, while scrutinizing the printed
matter in the room, noticed on a blank portion of a book cover
some very faint traces of faded writing. The finding of a small
bottle of iodine brought the question of secret writing in
"invisible" ink to the fore. Without attracting the attention
of any of those present D.S. Jones applied a little iodine to
a blank piece of paper found in a leather suitcase which was
being used as a repository for sundry books and papers. The
suspicion that the sheet was covered with secret writing proved
to be well founded, for a few strokes of the brush dipped in
the iodine preparation caused several Chinese characters to
appear. Following this test it was decided to take possession
of all literature in the room, subversive in character or
otherwise, including several harmless-looking sheets of Chinese
writing paper. These sheets of paper and the blank spaces in
between the lines of print on certain of the books were later
tested at the office by D.S.M. Coyne, using special chemical
reagents. A considerable quantity of secret writing was made
visible by this means. Translations of the writing revealed are
now being made and will be submitted when completed.
    A copy of a translation (only in parts is it literal) made
by D.S. Jones of an article written in French, dealing with
prison life in the French Municipal Gaol is also attached to
this report. The thorough knowledge of his subject is a good
indication that the author at some time or other was an
unwilling occupant of one of the cells at the gaol in question.

    在对迈尔赫路（Myburgh Road）239号的突袭行动进行期间，警佐琼斯（D.S. Jones）和职员宗（Zung）在仔细检查室内的印刷品时，注意到在一本书封面的空白部分有一些非常模糊的褪色字迹痕迹。发现一小瓶碘酒后，关于使用“隐形”墨水进行秘密书写的问题便凸显出来。为了不惊动在场的任何人，警佐琼斯将少许碘酒涂抹在一个皮箱内发现的一张白纸上，该皮箱当时被用作存放各类书籍和文件的容器。怀疑该纸张覆盖有秘密书写的想法被证实是有根据的，因为用蘸有碘酒制剂的毛笔刷了几下后，几个汉字显现出来。继此测试之后，决定没收室内所有具有颠覆性质或其他性质的文献，包括几张看起来无害的中文信纸。这些纸张以及某些书籍印刷行间的空白处，随后由警佐科因（D.S.M. Coyne）在办公室使用特殊化学试剂进行了测试。通过这种方法，大量秘密书写内容得以显现。目前正对显露出的文字进行翻译，完成后将提交。
    本报告还附有一份译文的副本（仅部分为直译），由警佐琼斯翻译，原文是一篇用法文写成的文章，涉及法公董局监狱的囚犯生活。作者对其主题的详尽了解很好地表明，该作者曾在某个时候成为上述监狱中某一牢房的不情愿居住者。

The composition of this article is so bad, and the grammar so
weak that it was only with the greatest difficulty and at the
cost of much effort that the meaning of the author could
be fathomed and a fair translation made. It is evident from
the style, or rather lack of style, that this is the work of a
Chinese with a very sketchy knowledge of the French language.
    The importance and the timeliness of these two raids with
the consequent four arrests cannot be too strongly stressed.
Documents taken possession of at the homes of the persons now
in custody show that the Communist Party was
planning to take advantage of the present deadlock in the
ricsha dispute to incite the thousands of ricsha pullers to
take the law into their own hands and perpetrate acts of
violence. The lack of incident -, which has been duly commented
on by the Press - at a time when it might fully be expected that
the radical element always present among large bodies of
unemployed men would become active, may, perhaps, be directly
ascribable to the timely apprehension of four agitators whose
detention by the Police has prevented them from developing the
subversive propaganda work among ricsha coolies for which plans
had already been drawn up.

这篇文章的构思如此糟糕，语法如此薄弱，以至于只有付出极大的努力和艰辛才能揣摩出作者的意思并做出尚可的翻译。从这种风格，或者说缺乏风格来看，这显然是一个法语知识非常肤浅的中国人所作。
    这两次突袭行动及其随之而来的四人被捕的重要性及及时性，无论怎样强调都不为过。从目前被拘留者家中查获的文件显示，共产党正计划利用当前人力车纠纷的僵局，煽动数千名人力车夫采取私刑并实施暴力行为。在此时期，人们完全有理由预期那些始终存在于大量失业人群中的激进分子会变得活跃，然而却未发生任何事件——这一点已得到新闻界的适当评论——这或许可以直接归因于及时逮捕了四名煽动者，警方的拘留阻止了他们按照既定计划在人力车苦力中开展颠覆性宣传工作。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT
Date April 1, 36.
Subject Seizure of subversive literature and arrest of Communist
suspects at House No.9, Lane 244 Singkeipang Road.
Made by D. S. Jones Forwarded by D.S.J cyne

The staff of S.2 having completed the examination
of the communistic matter seized at House No.9, Lane 241
Singkeipang Road on March 30, 1936, copies of the revised list,
giving where necessary a short account of the subject dealt
with in each document or leaflet, are forwarded together with
this report.

It may be seen from the literature in question that
the Chinese Communist Party still adheres to its old policy
of causing dissension between Capital and Labour and makes use
of every opportunity to assist the communist "struggle" by
means of demonstrations and labour strikes.

Article No.3 in the attached list is a manifesto
issued by the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese
Communist Youth League urging workers to demonstrate on behalf
of the disgruntled operatives of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill. It
also exhorts workers to form themselves into armed pickets for
purposes of self-defence and the protection of strikers and
workers connected with the so-called anti-Japanese and National
Salvation Movements.

The anti-Japanese feeling present among the Chinese
students renders them easily amenable to suggestions emanating
from radical sources that they can best gain their ends by
participating in demonstrations and engaging in other illegal
activities. Although there is no definite proof, it is quite
on the cards that the Chinese Communist Youth League has used
its influence to bring about the present student agitations in
local Chinese universities. Article 22 on the list refers to
a letter sent to the Futan University. This letter is not
available, but the fact that mention of it is made among the

制作人 D. S. Jones 转呈人 D.S.J cyne

S.2部门工作人员已完成对1936年3月30日在新加坡路241弄9号查获的共产主义材料的审查，现随本报告附上修订后的清单副本，必要时对每份文件或传单所涉及的主题作了简要说明。

从相关文献可以看出，中国共产党仍然坚持其制造资本与劳工之间不和的旧政策，并利用一切机会，通过示威和罢工来协助共产主义“斗争”。

附件清单中的第3项是一份宣言，由中国共产主义青年团江苏省委员会发布，敦促工人代表大康纱厂不满的工人举行示威。它还号召工人组成武装纠察队，以进行自卫并保护与所谓的抗日和救国运动有关的罢工者和工人。

中国学生中存在的反日情绪使他们很容易接受来自激进源头的建议，即他们可以通过参与示威和其他非法活动来最好地达到目的。虽然没有确凿的证据，但中国共产主义青年团利用其影响力促成当地中国大学目前的学生骚乱是完全有可能的。清单上的第22项提及一封寄往复旦大学的信件。这封信件并未找到，但在

List of Communist Literature seized at House 9,
Lane 244, Sing Kee Pang Road (K.R.District), at
10.10 p.m., March 30, 1936.

1) Communist newspaper entitled "The Youth's Truth
Newspaper" (or Shao Nyi Tsung Lee Pao), issue
No. 111, dated March 22, 1936, containing articles
of the usual communistic nature. 320 copies

2) Leaflet entitled "Manifesto addressed to the people
throughout the country, various political parties
and all troops, from the Chinese Communist Party,"
purporting to emanate from the Central Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party. It urges the people
and the military to unite, cease civil war, and fight
against the Japanese imperialists. 45 copies.

3) Leaflet entitled "Manifesto supporting the strike
of workers of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill," purporting
to emanate from the Kiangsu Provincial Committee
of the Chinese Communist Youth League, dated
February 8, 1936. It urges workers and others to
declare strikes and to hold demonstrations as a
protest against the "murder" of Mei Sz Chung, to collect
contributions for the relief of the workers of the
Dah Kong Cotton Mill who are on strike, and to
organize armed picketing corps and selfdefence corps
to protect strikers and others engaged in anti-Japanese
and national salvation movements. 26 copies

4) "The Youth's Truth Newspaper", issue No. 168
dated 28.2.36. One copy

5) ditto, extra issue dealing with the anniversary
of the Sino-Japanese conflict in Shanghai.
(dated 20.2.36). One copy

6) Manuscript of a short story entitled "MENUS",
describing the illtreatment of workers by the
management of a certain factory. One copy

7) Seven small receipts of the "Shanghai Mei Sz Chung
Tragedy Support Committee", for small sums of money
contributed by certain persons ranging from 10
coppers to 60 coppers.

8) Unused receipt book of "The National Salvation News
Agency." 3 copies

9) Leaflet containing a circular telegram, from the
commanders of the 1st and Second Anti-Japanese
Armies in North East (Manchuria) to various Government
officials, provincial authorities, commanders of
Government troops, commanders of Red Armies, and
public bodies throughout the country, etc. urging
them to unite and fight against Japan. One copy

10) Letter from "The Ricksha Coolies' Committee", undated,
(the name of the recipient has been cut out), dealing
with the following matters:-
(a) A meeting will be held by various societies to
discuss the organization of a national salvation
society.
(b) General meetings will be held in "Mutual Help
Sociation" on Foo Teh Road, Western District,
Hankow, Nanking Road, to discuss a reduction of
ricksha rent to 77 cents per day, to oppose Tang
Tung Ting of the Mutual Help Society who is
receiving $600. per month, and to urge the coolies
to besiege the S.M.C. & the Ricksha Owners Society
in order to force their demands.

1936年3月30日晚上10点10分，在新加坡路（新加坡区）244弄9号查获的共产党文献清单。

2) 传单，题为“中国共产党致全国同胞、各政党及各部队宣言”，声称出自中国共产党中央委员会。它呼吁人民和军队团结起来，停止内战，并对抗日本帝国主义。45份。

3) 传单，题为“支持大康纱厂工人罢工宣言”，声称出自中国共产主义青年团江苏省委员会，日期为1936年2月8日。它敦促工人和其他人宣布罢工并举行示威，以抗议“谋杀”梅世忠（Mei Sz Chung），为大康纱厂罢工工人募集救济捐款，并组织武装纠察队和自卫队，以保护罢工者及其他从事抗日和救国运动的人员。26份

Translation of a document found in the mouth of the
second accused named Zee Vung Ming, who was arrested
outside No.9, Lane 244 Singkeepang Road, at 10.20 p.m.
March 30, 1936.

District Committeemen, yesterday we held a mass meeting
at the Mutual Aid Association on Wu Tai Road. In compliance
with the methods mentioned in your letter we at first held
sectional meetings after which we asked our comrades to
arrange a mass meeting. We decided to appoint Han Chao-zai
(韩兆瑞) to demand that the hire charge be reduced to
seventy-seven cents, to oppose the refusal of the owners to
hire out their vehicles, to object to Chang Tung-ying receiving
a monthly pay of $420, and to demand the publication of the
accounts of the Mutual Aid Association. The meeting concluded
at 4.45 p.m. Our Comrade Kuo (郭 ) found thirty-seven
persons. There were more than one hundred persons on the
premises of the Mutual Aid Association. The Chief Secretary(?)
of the Wu Tai Road Mutual Aid Association told those present
not to talk loudly, whereupon some of our comrades wanted to
assault him. He did not interfere again.
The following persons were then appointed as delegates :-
Li Teh-hsia (李德夏) representing Kuo Chi Company.
Chang Dah-chu (張大軍) -do-
Fan Che-san (潘祝山) representing Fu Chi Company.
Woo Kuo-sze (吳國士) r -do-
Chen Siao-ziang (陳小祥) representing Kuk Chi Company.
Siao Mo (小馬 ) representing Chen Chi Company.
Kuo Sung-feng (郭松風) -do-
Yen Tso-ling (嚴左嶺) representing Chang Chi Company.
Chien Siao Wo-shang (錢小和尚) representing Low San Chi.
page_data.zh:
对1936年3月30日晚上10点20分在新加坡路（Singkeepang Road，音译）244弄9号外被捕的第二被告池云明（Zee Vung Ming，音译）口中发现文件的翻译。

各区委员，昨天我们在五台路互助会举行了一次群众大会。按照你们信中提到的方法，我们先举行了分部会议，随后请同志们安排群众大会。我们决定指派韩兆瑞（Han Chao-zai）提出要求将车租减至七角七分，反对车主拒绝出租车辆，反对张东英（Chang Tung-ying，音译）领取月薪420美元，并要求公布互助会的账目。会议于下午4点45分结束。我们的同志郭氏（Kuo）找到了三十七人。互助会现场有一百多人。五台路互助会的总干事（?）告诉在场的人不要大声说话，于是我们的一些同志想要殴打他。他不再干涉。
随后任命以下人员为代表：-
李德夏（Li Teh-hsia）代表国记公司（Kuo Chi Company）。
张大车（Chang Dah-chu） -同上-
潘祝山（Fan Che-san）代表福记公司（Fu Chi Company）。
吴国士（Woo Kuo-sze） r -同上-
陈小祥（Chen Siao-ziang）代表菊记公司（Kuk Chi Company）。
小马（Siao Mo）代表陈记公司（Chen Chi Company）。
郭松风（Kuo Sung-feng） -同上-
严左岭（Yen Tso-ling）代表张记公司（Chang Chi Company）。
钱小和尚（Chien Siao Wo-shang）代表老三记（Low San Chi）。

page_data.en:
-2-

Siao San-tse (小三子) representing Kwan Chi Company.

After the meeting, Lou Nyi Han (老倪韩) told me what
had happened. I told t'em to convene a meeting of the
representatives. Han Chao-zai was elected as chief
delegate.

Yao Ti (姚弟)
March 29.
page_data.zh:
-2-

小三子（Siao San-tse）代表关记公司（Kwan Chi Company）。

会后，老倪韩（Lou Nyi Han）告诉我发生了什么事。我让他们召开代表会议。韩兆瑞当选为首席代表。

姚弟（Yao Ti）
3月29日。

对1936年3月30日晚上10点20分在新加坡路（Singkeepang Road，音译）244弄9号外被捕的第二被告池云明（Zee Vung ming，音译）口中发现文件的翻译。

各区委员，昨天我们在五台路互助会举行了一次群众大会。按照你们信中提到的方法，我们先举行了分部会议，随后请同志们安排群众大会。我们决定指派韩兆瑞（Han Chao-zai）（韓兆瑞）提出要求将车租减至七角七分，反对车主拒绝出租车辆，反对张东英（Chang Tung-ying，音译）领取月薪420美元，并要求公布互助会的账目。会议于下午4点45分结束。我们的同志郭氏（Kuo）找到了三十七人。互助会现场有一百多人。五台路互助会的总干事（?）告诉在场的人不要大声说话，于是我们的一些同志想要殴打他。他不再干涉。
随后任命以下人员为代表：-
李德夏（Li Teh-hsia）代表国记公司（Kue Chi Company）。
张大车（Chang Dah-chu） -同上-

郭仁凤（Kuo Sung-feng） -同上-
严子俊（Yen Tso-ling）代表张记公司（Chang Chi Company）。
钱小和生（Chien Siao Wo-sheng）代表兰海记（Lan Hae Chi）。

had happened. I told them to convene a meeting of the
representatives. Han Chao-zai was elected as chief
delegate.

Yao Ti (姚弟)

姚弟（Yao Ti）

Life in Prison 


The Prison : Last year this prison was handed over to the 
Nanking overnment, but the power is still in the hands of the 
French imperialists. The occupants of the gaol are arrested and 
handed over by the French Police. Everything in the prison 
d>-rends on French imperialists. This is the reason why the 
frrisoners in this prison are much worse treated than those in 
other prisons. When the prison belonged to French imperialists 
there were only 800 prisoners; now there ure more than 2000. 
In this we see that the Kuomintang, in order to keep in with 
the imperialists, end*avours to persecute the people. The 
rréson can only contain 800 prisoners, but now it is more than 
a third (sic). During the present hot weather eight men ire shut 
up ina little room where they cannot stretch their legs. The 
air is insupportable; the meals are very bad. Nine-tenths are 
sick. in winter tips is no mattress anderneath and no covering 
on tor. All day o hears nothing byt the noise of blows with 
the fists and batons, and the groans of the sick. 


The Life: For food we are paid 16 sous a day; but owing to the 
grafting habits of the Director of the prison, we don't draw so 
much as 10 sous a day. The rice we eat is mixed with many other 
things; with pieces of very bad vegetable. It is said that one 
can eat meat, Sut the meat supplied often causes terrible sickness. 
One is allowed only one bath a week and one wash a day.Bighteen 
hundred reople wash in the same water. .he one who washes last 
has to use water which gives off the same vile odour as that in 
street sewers. A man is set to watch the water and whenever 
anyone approaches for a wash he shouts "QuicklylQuicklylquickly!" 
Three minutes only is allowed for a wash. Some who come to dip 
their hands in the water are driven away, beaten or insulted. 
Five times a week we are allowed 15 minutes for recreation, but 
we do not always get this 15 minutes. But the White Russians 

are given recreation six times a week, each period of recreation 
lasting one. hour and a half. Not only are they better off in 

this respect, but they are also allowed 70 sous a day for food. 


Persecution : Not only do the prisoners live wretchedly, they 
also undergo terrible treatment. Robbers are usually tied by the 
legs at the order of the French imperialists. Practically every 
day they are beaten on the hands ami feet with sticks. If they 
try to defend themselves they are persecuted in the manner 
handed down by Chinese ancestors. Last year a poor wretch who 
broke an ordure bucket was punished in this fashion. Many others 
also receive this same punishment. Many commit suicide. On May 6 
last year a prisoner, tieing his legs with No. 181 named : 
CHANG WA SIN because of a serious illness spoke wildly being 
lmown by the Ohief of Police and the Secretary of the Prison; 
they stopped the poor wretch Up with iron and the next day hé 
had lost four teeth (sic). He lost much blood and not long 
after he was dead. His comrade in the prison kept the four | 
teeth as a souvenir. To end our misfortune vece nee Sper spat

into this hospital. 


The conflict of the Prisoners : To protect their lives all the 
unfortunates in prison get together and oppose persecution. On 
March 17 of this year everyone gave a united shout to oppose 
persecution. This shout terrified the Police of the French 
Concession and they sent a large number of their men to watch us. 
The Director of the prison yielded to Hour agitation and accepted 
all our demands. Not long after, though, four hundred of our 
comrades were sent to other places far from Shanghai. On August 
lst 1933the Director was changed. The new Director was worse 

than the old. Many are persecuted. We cannot talk out loud. On 
August 24, 1933 a prisoner on the 2nd floor was put in another. 
room and had his legs tied and feet fastened. All the comrades on 
the 2nd floor got very angry and shouted loud their protests. 

Tre Director, more terrible than ever, tied the legs of three 
others. On the evening of the same day all prisoners on the 2nd 
and 4th floors were tied by the legs and they all shouted loudly 
together. The Director ordered all the Police to strike and kick. 
At this moment only groans and cries of suffering could be heard. 
Persecution such as this is not only to be found in prisons but 
in the whole of China. 


The life of the gaolers and police : Altogether there are more 
than forty police and sixty gaolers in the prison. Most of these 
come from villages. Some took part in the revolution of 1927. 
They spend a laborious life. The monthly salary is about ten 
dollars. When absent through sickness a deduction is made from 
their salary. They get no time off for holidays. They follow one- 
another on day and night duty and they have to do other work. 
They can be pumished or dismissed by their superiors. There is 
no bed in which they can sleep and their food is bad. In addition 
there are thirty men employed to take the place of those absent. 
These get their food but no wages. They are good, especially to 
political prisoners. Not long ago get Big mretne an increase of 
salary; that a bed be supplied, and t special work be 
abolished. Their request for a bed was granted, but the bedhas 
not yet been suprlied.
